bugs.summary: as.list(<environment>) returns misaligned names/values (or an internal SET_VECTOR_ELT error) when an active binding modifies the environment

comments.creator: 0599jiangyc
comments.text:
The following code:

```
e <- new.env()
e$x <- "X"; e$y <- "Y"
makeActiveBinding("a", function() { if (exists("y", e, inherits = FALSE)) rm("y", envir = e); "A" }, e)
str(as.list(e, sorted = TRUE))
```

Resulted in this output (no error, wrong result: `a` gets the value of the removed `y`, and `"A"` is lost):

```
List of 2
 $ a: chr "Y"
 $ x: chr "X"
```

If the active binding instead *adds* a variable, `as.list()` fails with an internal error:

```
e <- new.env()
makeActiveBinding("a", function() { assign("b", 1, envir = e); 1 }, e)
x <- as.list(e)
```

```
Error in as.list.environment(e) :
  attempt to set index 1/1 in SET_VECTOR_ELT
Calls: as.list -> as.list.environment
```

(with `new.env(hash = FALSE)` the error is `attempt to set index 1/1 in SET_STRING_ELT`).

`do_env2list()` (src/main/envir.c) computes the length of the environment, allocates `names` and `ans`, then fills the values with `FrameValues()`/`HashTableValues()`, and fills the names in a second pass. Filling the values forces active bindings (and promises), which can run arbitrary R code that changes the environment between the sizing step and the two fill passes. Growth runs into the bounds check in SET_VECTOR_ELT/SET_STRING_ELT. Shrinkage leaves the names and values out of step without any error. `eapply()` and `mget()` might be affected in the same way; I have not checked them.

A possible fix: collect the bindings (symbols and binding cells) first, then force the values, or re-check the length after forcing and signal a proper R-level error.

Reproduced on R-devel and on R 4.6.1:

```
Rscript --vanilla ./min.R
```

Commit:
```
R-devel r90659 (r-devel/r-svn cf22bdf, 2026-10-10); also R 4.6.1 (Docker r-base:latest)
```

Build configuration:
```
../configure CC="clang-18 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer" CXX="clang++-18 -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer" \
  FC=gfortran F77=gfortran CFLAGS="-O1 -g" CXXFLAGS="-O1 -g" \
  --enable-strict-barrier --with-recommended-packages=no \
  --with-x=no --with-tcltk=no --with-cairo=no --with-aqua=no \
  --disable-java --disable-nls --disable-openmp
(also stock R 4.6.1 from the r-base Docker image)
```

Operating System:
```
Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Docker), x86_64
```

*First part*

Reformatted the code 

 (Apologies that markdown code fencing isn't completely working for me here)




``` 
# Original code
    e <- new.env() 
    e$x <- "X"  
    e$y <- "Y"  


    makeActiveBinding("a", function() {   
        if (exists("y", e, inherits = FALSE)) {  
            rm("y", envir = e)  
          } else {  
           "A"   
          }  
        },  
       e)  
   str(as.list(e, sorted = TRUE))  

```



List of 2
  $ a: chr "Y"  
  $ x: chr "X"  


Looking at the condition in the function


```
# Condition
   e <- new.env()
   e$x <- "X"
   e$y <- "Y"

   exists("y", e, inherits = FALSE)

```

TRUE

So I'd be expecting the "y" to be removed.  Can you clarify what I am misunderstanding? 




*For the second part* 

```
e <- new.env()
makeActiveBinding("a", function() {     
       assign("b", 1, envir = e)
        1 }, 
        e)



```

As written I get the same error. I think the problem comes from having the
envir parameter set in the `assign()` to the same name as the `makeActiveBinding()` parameter.

```
makeActiveBinding("a", function() {     
   assign("b", 1)
     1 }, 
     e)
as.list(e)
```
> $a
>  [1] 1

Which I think is what you are expecting.   I think that the problem is happening when e is used twice. 


```
 e <- new.env()
 f <- new.env() 
makeActiveBinding("a", function() {     
    assign("b", 1, envir = f)
    1 }, 
    e)
as.list(e)
```
> $a
> [1] 1

```
 as.list(f)
```
> $b
> [1] 1

I have to say, I'm not really sure what I would expect in this case, but I think it is pointing to where the problem is happening. 
If nothing else, I'd expect a clear error message.
